utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-80-I, the Prosecutor against Zdravko Tolimir, Radivoje Miletic and Milan Gvero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: This is the further initial appearance of Mr. Radivoje Miletic. Mr. Miletic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MILETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Can that be looked after? We were having a problem of that kind this morning as well. Can you understand me now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MILETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: May we have the appearances now, the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Peter McCloskey and accompanied by Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Peter Morrissey, and I appear as counsel -- in the capacity of duty counsel today, on behalf of Mr. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On the strength of the order given on the 14th March by Judge Agius who conducted the Initial Appearance on the 2nd of March, I have become the Pre-Trial Judge in your case. As was explained to you during your initial appearance, you do have the right to remain silent; in other words, no one can force to you say anything. Mr. Miletic, I would like to remind you that at the initial appearance, you chose not to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty. According to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence in such a case, you are called upon to enter a plea within 30 days of the initial appearance, which is today, and which is the reason why we have gathered again to enable you to do so. I will now proceed to conduct the procedure part of the further initial appearance of the accused Mr. Radivoje Miletic pursuant to Article -- to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. First of all, Mr. Miletic, I need to ensure that you are represented, and I take it that you are -- I take note that you are represented today by Mr. Morrissey. Do you have anything to say about your being represented by Mr. Morrissey today, Mr. Miletic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MILETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have any matters to raise in regard to my representation by Mr. Morrissey. I am quite satisfied. I am just concerned about this problem that seems to have arisen concerning my Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Indeed. As I have understood, there are problems with the appointment of your Defence counsel, but I've been told that these problems will be resolved in the next few days so that your counsel would be assigned to you in the course of the following few days, at the very latest at the end of next week. So given that situation, there are two things -- two ways in which we can proceed today. Either you will decide to plead today and we can proceed with today's initial appearance. In the alternative, we could decide in to adjourn, in which case then there would be a further initial appearance on the moment when you will have appointed -- or when counsel would have been assigned to you. So that is up to you now to decide what you prefer to be the case, to be the option.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I assist the Court here, the Tribunal here, if I may. I've taken some instruction from Mr. Miletic on this topic. Your Honour of course can confirm this with him, but it assist if I put what I understand to be the position. Mr. Miletic would like the matter to be adjourned for that period of time. On the 5th of April, he has arranged a meeting, a conference with counsel. He's already spoken to a number of counsel, and he feels that he would be able to make a choice between those in a sensible way once he's spoken to the individual that he is meeting on the 5th of April. Therefore, there is no need for a lengthy adjournment, but he would be grateful if it were possible to adjourn the matter to allow him to have that meeting and then thereafter to come to this Court and having being properly advised by counsel who knows something about the case, and that's certainly not myself, I have to say, and he would be in a position then to meaningfully plead to the indictment or to meaningfully to raise any objections to the indictment that he might want to raise in the next 30-day period. Could I just indicate that it's likely that he would want to traverse the indictment and that the starting of time to run, for him to be allowed to do that, commences at the time when he enters that plea. In other words, once he's pleaded, he has then 30 days only in which to present the relevant arguments. And if he pleaded today, time would commence running when he still wasn't represented and still not able to meaningfully deal with that question. So for those reasons, he has indicated to me that that's the course he'd like. He would like the appearance to be adjourned for 14 days to enable him to see this person that he wants to see on the 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So what you are proposing is that the 30 days for the Article 72 submissions would start running on the moment of the further initial appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it should start running on the time he enters his plea and presumably that once he's got counsel in the case who can read material, who can stay in the case and who can meaningfully contribute, then he will be in a position to enter a plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Because there's also another possibility for those 30 days to start running on the moment that the Prosecution has submitted the -- has disclosed the material on the basis of Article 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's really the concern we have here. And that's part of the reason why it can't be resolved with one stroke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It also depends on when the Prosecution makes that disclosure. I may perhaps turn to the Prosecution now to see what the position is on your side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it's -- the rule is that 30 days begins after we have given the General the disclosure. He, I know, is aware of this, we discussed it last time and he chose naturally, I think, not to get to the material. And the date -- our deadline is tomorrow, so we've got the material, we're ready to give it to him. However, if he doesn't want to get it yet, he wants to give his lawyer some extra time and he wants to resolve this next week, I see no problem for him waiving that 30 days and he can get it when he sorts out his lawyer. I think the most important thing is to get him enough time to get a lawyer he's comfortable with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you for that. So you would be in a position to submit the material, say, within two or three days after you have been noticed of the fact that counsel has been assigned to Mr. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can give it to him now if he wants, or any time he wants it, given a reasonable time. I think he can waive his pleaing now and he can waive right now receiving the material as long as it happens in a reasonable time and according to Mr. Morrissey and yourself, that time is next week, then that's fine with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So would it be possible then to suggest that counsel be assigned by next Friday at the very latest and that on that moment, the Prosecution will proceed to the disclosure of the material? Does that sound acceptable to both sides?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask for it to be 14 days because if he sees this person -- I'm just aware of human frailty and that there's the idea that they're going to meet on that day, that's the plan, that's the appointment. If somebody misses a plan or if somebody -- if there is a difficulty on that day, then we find ourselves with a deadline that can't be handled, and therefore I ask that the time period not be next Friday but the following Friday. If that were possible, then that would also allow counsel who were chosen to have some period of time to familiarise themselves with the contents of the indictment. I presume that those he has spoken to have some familiarity with it but, you know, a few days of solid work would no doubt assist in that regard. So that's what our submission is, that if the matter could be adjourned to be 14 days, that means the choice could be made not with an excess of time but in a way that was relaxed and comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So what you're suggesting is that the clock for the 30 days starts ticking not on the moment as you were saying previously of the further initial appearance but two weeks from now, which would be more or less one week after the counsel has been assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Look, I apologise, I think it was lack of clarity originally. Really what I would submit is that the whole thing should take place in 14 days. The next initial appearance should be in 14 days' time, if that's possible. And on that day, that the Prosecution -- we would then accept service of the materials. It could be indicated to the Tribunal at that time that counsel have been appointed and that the proceedings could commence and time periods could start running on that date. I'm just concerned, Your Honour, if the time limit was imposed at the end of next week, it makes it very tight if something went wrong in this conference or if the person didn't come or if there was some difficulty that arose, we'd then have to mention the matter and seek an ad hoc adjournment at that time. It seems better to allow Mr. Miletic to -- to just allow him that one extra week and then hopefully the matter will proceed smoothly at that time. So, yes. I apologise for not being a little clearer earlier but that really is our application, that the matter -- this matter now be adjourned for two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Morrissey suggesting the violation of several rules, all of which are designed to protect his client and so I don't have any objection. 14 days sounds fine. I think his client with waive those rules and -- no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then, we will instruct the Registrar to set a new date for an initial appearance two weeks from now. And then we can adjourn for today unless there are any further matters that counsel would wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: at 4.31 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Further Appearance is adjourned
